newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore information technology sales to rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore information technology sales to rise.

text.p: Singapore sales of information technology (IT) equipment are expected to shoot up by 30 percent annually in 1996 and 1997, Singapore's National Computer Board (NCB) said on Tuesday.
The NCB said total sales of information technology like computer hardware, computer software and services in 1995 rose to US$6.73 billion from $5.0 billion in 1994.
"The high growth was driven primarily by a strong export market which grew more than twice as fast as the domestic market," it said in a survey of the Singapore IT industry.

"The industry expects the high growth achieved in 1995 to continue into 1996 and 1997, with growth rates of over 30 percent projected for the overall information technology industry," the report said.
A softening of the export market may hit sales in 1997, but this can be offset by a substantial increase in the domestic sales growth rate.

"The industry is thus projecting a consolidation in the growth of the hardware sector, both locally and overseas, while expecting further expansion in the more valued-added software and information technology services sector,"
Hardware sales, nearly half of them involving the sale of personal computers, accounted for 75.7 percent of total industry sales in 1995, the NCB report said.
Information services like customised software development and technical support accounted for 13.2 percent of total sales. The remaining 11.1 percent was made up by sales of computer software.
